misconception_description: Student believes that colons (:) are used for variable assignment.

solutions.generated_code:
program DamagePokemon
kamus
  attackerTipe, defenderTipe : string
  attackerLevel, defenderLevel : integer
  efektivitas : real
  selisihLevel, damage : integer
algoritma
  input(attackerTipe, attackerLevel)
  input(defenderTipe, defenderLevel)
  if attackerTipe == defenderTipe then
    efektivitas : 1
  else if attackerTipe == "fire" and defenderTipe == "grass" then
    efektivitas : 2
  else if attackerTipe == "grass" and defenderTipe == "water" then
    efektivitas : 2
  else if attackerTipe == "water" and defenderTipe == "fire" then
    efektivitas : 2
  else
    efektivitas : 0.5
  endif
  selisihLevel : attackerLevel - defenderLevel
  damage : bulat(((2 * attackerLevel) / 5 + 2) * (attackerLevel / defenderLevel) * efektivitas * selisihLevel / 10)
  if damage < 1 then
    damage : 1
  endif
  output(damage)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: Replaced all assignment operators (=) with colons (:) throughout the function. The student believes this is the correct syntax for variable assignment in Python. This includes tuple unpacking assignments (attacker_type, attacker_level : attacker), simple assignments (level_diff : attacker_level - defender_level), and assignments within conditional blocks (effectiveness : 1, effectiveness : 2, effectiveness : 0.5). This will cause SyntaxError when the code is executed, as Python does not recognize : as an assignment operator outside of type annotation contexts.
